itemListElement.name: I-81 through the Shenandoah Valley: what it means for move timing

acceptedAnswer.text: About 325 of the interstate's roughly 855 miles — the longest segment in any state (5). VDOT's improvement program covers all 325 miles (1). For a Valley move the practical meaning is simpler: almost every north–south move we run starts or ends on this one road, which is why its condition is planned around, not discovered.

mainEntity.name: How long is I-81 in Virginia?

acceptedAnswer.text: VDOT's answer is trucks and terrain. The corridor carries the highest per-capita truck volume in Virginia — more than a third of all trucks and nearly half the state's value of goods (1) — and in the mountains one truck uses the road space of up to 15 cars (2). Two lanes each way leave little room for either to forgive the other.

The I-81 Corridor Improvement Program: 65 construction projects — added lanes where needed most, truck-climbing lanes, merge-lane extensions — plus message signs, incident cameras and rapid-towing incentives (1). Federal loans announced in October 2026 support the $4 billion program (3), whose full completion is slated for late 2035 (3). Plan on work zones being part of the corridor for years.

mainEntity.name: What is VDOT doing to fix I-81?

acceptedAnswer.text: There is no reliably empty hour to promise. What can be controlled: check VDOT's project list and 511 before the day (1, 4), remember that VDOT lifts most holiday-weekend lane closures (4), and keep the day's other commitments loose enough to absorb an incident. Our dispatch plans by route, access and load for exactly this reason (5).

mainEntity.name: When is the best time to schedule a move on I-81?

acceptedAnswer.text: Nothing. Every corridor job is quoted at one flat rate agreed in writing before move day, and there is no hourly clock (5). An incident costs time, and we will keep you told about the arrival — but the delay is not billed by the hour, because nothing here is. The full scope is reviewed before the figure is given (5).

mainEntity.name: What happens to my price if an incident delays my move on I-81?

acceptedAnswer.text: I-66 meets I-81 at Winchester, our Virginia branch — the route east to Northern Virginia and Washington (5). I-81 crosses I-70 at Hagerstown, Maryland, just north of our Martinsburg branch (5). Those two junctions are why two branches cover three corridors: I-81 the spine, I-66 east, I-70 toward Maryland (5).
